entities.summary: Jacques-François Lefranc was a French cleric and prominent anti-Masonic author, writing extensively against Freemasonry's influence in France during the late 18th century. His works, such as 'The History of Freemasonry' (1778), aimed to expose the perceived dangers of Masonic societies and their impact on French society. Lefranc's writings contributed to the growing tensions between Freemasons and the general public, ultimately influencing the French Revolution's anti-Masonic fervor. The movement's climax came in 1786, when the French National Assembly passed a decree outlawing Freemasonry, with Lefranc's works seen as instrumental in shaping public opinion. This pivotal moment in French history highlights the intersection of religion, politics, and social change during the late Enlightenment period. Lefranc's legacy lies in his role as a vocal critic of Masonic societies, his contributions to the French Revolution's anti-Masonic movement, and his impact on the broader cultural and historical narrative of late 18th-century France.
